<thought>We need to determine how many carbonyl (C=O) groups are present in the unknown compound. The most direct way is to look at the 13C NMR spectrum, where carbonyl carbons appear in the downfield region (~190‑220 ppm). By counting the distinct peaks in that region we can infer the number of carbonyl carbons, which equals the number of C=O groups. I will request the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
